newsitem.title: UK: Oriental Restaurant Grp. set for 14.7 mln stg float.
newsitem.headline: Oriental Restaurant Grp. set for 14.7 mln stg float.

text.p: The City, London's financial heart, will find its appetite for oriental food spiced up further next week when Oriental Restaurant Group makes a placing valuing the company at 14.7 million stg ($23 million).

The group, which runs four specialist eateries in London and a wholesale grocery business, said in a statement on Wednesday that 2.6 million shares would be placed at 154 pence each, with dealings expected to start on October 3.

Oriental runs Sri Siam City and Imperial City, both based in London's financial district, Sri Siam Soho, its first restaurant which opened in 1988 in central London and Sri Thai, based in Victoria, near the Houses of Parliament.
The flotation would provide the resources for developing the restaurant group's "proven formula" and allowing for its next period of expansion, managing director Hock Ann Chua said.
Sri Siam City was the City's first Thai restaurant when it opened in September 1991, the company said, with seating for 135 diners.
Imperial City, based in the Royal Exchange in the centre of the City, has been described as "the best Chinese in the City" by the 1996 "Square Meal" City-based restaurant guide.
Sri Thai was opened in September 1995, making it the youngest member of the chain.
The company's wholesale division, through Chuanglee Limited, supplies Thai restaurants within the confines of the M25 orbital motorway which runs round greater London.
Oriental said it saw "considerable opportunities to widen the cuisine and style of trading," and would be looking for "green-field" sites primarily to expand its restaurant chain.
It is in talks for leases of additional premises in the City and West End of London and said proceeds of the flotation would be used in part to fit out new restaurants.
Oriental said performance in the current financial year was ahead of budget, with Sri Siam Soho exceeding expectations.

In the year ending March 31, 1996, Oriental saw pretax profits of 664,000 pounds on turnover of 4.49 million pounds, with earnings per share calculated at 8.2 pence or 12.3 pence on an adjusted basis.
